events.headline: First US-Russia-Ukraine Trilateral Talks Since February Open in Abu Dhabi
events.summary: Negotiators from Russia, Ukraine and the US opened two days of talks in Abu Dhabi on ending the war, post-war security guarantees and reconstruction — the first full trilateral session since talks were suspended in February amid the Iran conflict, building on the Kherson-ceasefire discussions hosted by Melania Trump at the White House. UK, French, German, Italian, NATO and EU officials held parallel side meetings with the Ukrainian delegation.

events.headline: Israel's President Gives Eisenkot First Chance to Form Next Government Over Netanyahu
events.summary: President Isaac Herzog formally gave Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form Israel's next government, after 67 members of the Knesset backed him versus 46 for Netanyahu. Eisenkot has up to 28 days, extendable by 14, and has called for an 'emergency government.'

events.headline: Indonesia Names Fourth Wiretapping Suspect as 20,000+ Troops Secure Jakarta Amid Widodo Hearing
events.summary: Indonesian police named a fourth suspect, Slamet Uliandi, a former IT/monitoring chief at the Criminal Investigation Agency, in the scandal over wiretapping of President Prabowo. Authorities deployed over 20,000 troops and police to Jakarta amid a defamation hearing involving former president Joko Widodo.

events.headline: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Climbs to 10,741 Cases and 5,230 Deaths; Spread to Kenya and Nigeria Confirmed
events.summary: As of Nov 5, WHO's Disease Outbreak News confirms 10,741 cases and 5,230 deaths from the Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak, up from 10,563/5,130 reported Oct 29. The case fatality ratio is about 48.7%; the outbreak spans 67+ health zones across 8 provinces with confirmed spread to Kenya and Nigeria.

events.headline: Former Paraguayan President Peña Charged, Detained at Military Facility Over Ueno Bank Collapse
events.summary: Following his Senate removal on Nov 6, prosecutors charged former President Santiago Peña with breach of trust and misuse of public funds tied to the Ueno Bank collapse. A judge ordered him held at a military facility pending trial; Peña denies wrongdoing and is appealing.

events.headline: Death Toll From Russian Strike on Komyshuvakha Aid Site Rises to 55
events.summary: The Nov 2 Russian strike on a school used as a humanitarian aid-distribution point in Komyshuvakha has seen its confirmed death toll climb to 55 per Ukraine's State Emergency Service, up from nearly 40 reported Nov 3. Rescuers continue pulling bodies from rubble in what is now the deadliest single attack on Zaporizhzhia Oblast civilians of the war.

events.headline: US Measles Outbreak Surpasses 5,000 Cases, Highest Count Since 1991
events.summary: The CDC confirmed 5,182 measles cases in 2026 across 46 states, the highest total since the US eliminated domestic transmission, driven by declining vaccination rates; several deaths have been reported this year, almost entirely among unvaccinated individuals. Officials warn the outbreak threatens the country's 'measles elimination' status.

events.headline: Pennsylvania Confirms Sixth Measles-Linked Death as Nation's Largest Outbreak in Decades Grows
events.summary: Pennsylvania health officials confirmed on Nov. 4, 2026 that an unvaccinated Jefferson County resident became the state's sixth measles-associated death this year. The statewide outbreak has grown to more than 1,467 cases, the largest in the US in more than 30 years.

events.headline: Myanmar Junta Airstrikes Kill Civilians in Rakhine State as Arakan Army Advances Near Sittwe
events.summary: Myanmar military airstrikes across four Rakhine townships killed at least 12 civilians and injured 32 on Nov 1, part of an intensifying junta offensive launched in September. The Arakan Army has advanced to within roughly 2km of Sittwe, pressing an assault on the junta's naval base there.

events.headline: EU Activates Emergency Civil Protection Mechanism as Russian Strikes Keep Battering Ukraine's Power Grid
events.summary: Russian forces struck four electrical substations across Kyiv, Dnipropetrovsk, Cherkasy and Vinnytsia regions on Nov 9, compounding the damage from the Nov 8 strikes on Kyiv's bridge and power grid. The European Commission and Ukrainian officials convened to deploy the EU Civil Protection Mechanism for emergency power, heating and water assistance ahead of winter.

events.headline: Oregon's Record 2026 Wildfire Season Officially Ends After Burning 2.5 Million Acres at $311.5 Million Cost
events.summary: The Oregon Department of Forestry lifted fire restrictions statewide around Nov. 5, closing the state's record-breaking 2026 wildfire season at a final tally of roughly 2.5 million acres burned (up from the ~2 million acre figure reported earlier in the season) and gross suppression costs of about $311.5 million. Two firefighters died this season battling the Austin Fire and Wrights Springs Fire in Klamath County.

events.headline: 3M Agrees to Pay Up to $7.35 Billion to Settle 'Forever Chemical' Contamination Claims
events.summary: 3M agreed on Nov. 4-5, 2026 to pay up to $7.35 billion over nine years to settle PFAS personal-injury claims brought by roughly 120,000 plaintiffs near military bases and airports. The company made no admission of wrongdoing in the settlement.

events.headline: Newsom Moves to Commute All 548 California Death Sentences to Life Without Parole
events.summary: Gov. Gavin Newsom announced he will commute every death sentence in California, affecting 548 people on the Western Hemisphere's largest death row, to life without parole. The move comes about eight years after he imposed an execution moratorium; the California Supreme Court must still approve roughly 382 of the commutations involving repeat felons.

events.headline: Houthis Capture Al-Majza'a in Lahej as Airstrike on Taiz Market Kills About 30
events.summary: Airstrikes hit the al-Hadara market in al-Waziyah, Taiz, killing at least 30 people; Houthi officials blamed Saudi-led coalition aircraft, while the Yemeni government blamed a Houthi ballistic missile and called it a war crime. Separately, Houthi forces captured the town of Al-Majza'a in Lahej Governorate, expanding their territorial control.

events.headline: WHO Warns Violence in Northern Ethiopia Is Pushing Health System Toward Collapse
events.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros warned that renewed fighting between Tigrayan forces and Addis Ababa, plus drone strikes, is pushing Ethiopia's health system in the north toward collapse. He cited shortages of health workers and medicine and limited ambulance access, amid deteriorating Ethiopia-Eritrea relations over reported Eritrean military incursions.

events.headline: Israeli Strike Kills Three Sisters and Grandmother in Aynata, Southern Lebanon
events.summary: An Israeli strike hit a civilian car traveling between the villages of Aynata and Aitaroun, killing three sisters (ages 10-14) and their grandmother; their mother survived and was hospitalized. The strike, amid continued Israeli demolition and search operations in southern Lebanon, sparked domestic outrage over a possible violation of international law.

events.headline: Simultaneous El Niño and La Niña Flooding Displaces Over 158,000 Across Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay and Colombia
events.summary: El Niño-driven Paraná and Uruguay River flooding has forced mass evacuations across northeastern Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay, while La Niña-driven rains simultaneously flood much of Colombia. Combined, the disasters have displaced more than 158,000 people and killed at least 16; Argentina's Entre Ríos province saw the Uruguay River reach its highest level in nearly a century.

events.headline: Pope Leo XIV Delivers Veiled Rebuke of Milei's Austerity Program During Argentina Visit
events.summary: On the first papal visit to Argentina in nearly four decades, Pope Leo XIV told President Javier Milei that economic growth 'must benefit all' and that leaders must prioritize people over economic metrics, a pointed but diplomatic critique of Milei's austerity cuts. Milei, who has previously clashed rhetorically with the Vatican, greeted the pope cordially.

events.headline: Haiti's '400 Mawozo' Gang Leader Formally Reaches Out to UN and Disarmament Commission for Peace Talks
events.summary: 400 Mawozo gang leader Wilson Joseph wrote to the UN Secretary-General and Haiti's National Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration Commission requesting dialogue and a pause in operations, amid an intensified security push involving 2,500 Salvadoran troops deployed since late October. A rival gang leader, Mathias Saintil, was separately killed Nov 5 in a strike by Haitian police and allied forces.

events.headline: France Protests Turn Violent as Up to 250,000 March in Fourth Weekend of Cost-of-Living Unrest
events.summary: Between 146,000 and 250,000 people protested nationwide in France on Nov 7, including about 46,000 in Paris, marking a fourth straight weekend of cost-of-living demonstrations. Police used tear gas in Paris, 360 people were arrested, and roughly 70,000 security personnel were deployed.

events.headline: US Evacuates Aircraft From Second UK Base, RAF Mildenhall, as Iran Tensions Persist After Qeshm Strikes
events.summary: The US military evacuated refueling tankers and other aircraft from RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk following an Iran-linked threat, relocating assets to Germany — the second UK base, after RAF Fairford, from which US aircraft have been pulled amid continued Hormuz-blockade tensions following strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island.

events.headline: Ukrainian Drones Strike Kirishi Refinery, Russia's Second-Largest, Extending Energy Campaign
events.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the Kirishinefteorgsintez (KINEF) refinery in Russia's Leningrad Oblast, sparking fires; a woman was killed in nearby Vsevolozhsk by debris from an intercepted drone. It is the latest in Ukraine's expanding campaign against Russian energy infrastructure, following last week's strike on the Saratov refinery.

events.headline: Sand Embankment Collapse Kills Five in Flooded Gaza Tent Camp Amid Winter Storm
events.summary: A sand embankment collapsed onto tents sheltering displaced families in southern Deir al-Balah, Gaza, killing five people including a woman and children. The collapse came amid a multi-day storm that has flooded roughly 70,000 tents across Gaza and damaged more than 2,000 buildings.

events.headline: Houthi Strike Debris Damages Riyadh Financial District Building; Group Claims Yemen Terminal Hit
events.summary: A Houthi spokesman claimed responsibility for missile and drone strikes targeting King Khalid International Airport, oil storage tanks and an Aramco facility in Riyadh on Nov 8. Saudi air defenses intercepted missiles, but debris damaged a building in the King Abdullah Financial District; the group separately claimed a strike on the Ras Isa oil terminal in Yemen.

events.headline: US Calls China's Coast Guard Standoff With Taiwan Near Pratas Islands 'Deeply Destabilizing'
events.summary: Taiwan's coast guard confronted a Chinese coast guard vessel that entered restricted waters near the Pratas Islands, coming within 1 nautical mile of a Taiwanese ship before being told to leave — part of a pattern of Chinese incursions near Pratas in 2026. A US State Department spokesperson called China's actions 'deeply destabilizing', amid China's broader naval buildup of 100+ vessels near Taiwan.

events.headline: Tanzanian Opposition Leader Tundu Lissu Acquitted of Treason, Convicted of Incitement
events.summary: A Tanzanian court acquitted opposition leader Tundu Lissu of treason on Nov 6 but convicted him of incitement, sentencing him to four years in prison. Lissu had been detained for more than 18 months since his April 2025 arrest, and rights groups and the UN have called the case politically motivated.

events.headline: US Military Conducts New Lethal Strikes on Suspected Drug Boats in Caribbean
events.summary: US forces carried out additional strikes against vessels suspected of smuggling narcotics in the Caribbean near Venezuela, continuing SOUTHCOM's 'Southern Spear' campaign that has killed over 235 people in 70+ strikes since September 2025. Lawmakers and Colombian/Venezuelan officials have disputed the intelligence behind the targeting claims.

events.headline: Colombia Attributes Deadly Drone Attack on Military Base to ELN, Links It to New US Reaper Drone Operations
events.summary: Colombian authorities formally attributed the Nov 7 drone attack that killed three soldiers and wounded 8-16 at an army base in Santa Rosa del Sur, Bolívar, to the ELN; reporting links the strike to the recent operational debut of US-supplied MQ-9 Reaper drones in the region. President de la Espriella vowed retaliation. The specific ELN attribution comes from a specialist outlet and is pending wider confirmation from a major wire service.
events.locationName: Santa Rosa del Sur, Bolívar, Colombia

events.headline: Kabila-Led FRN Takes Over DRC-M23 Doha Peace Talks, Threatens Withdrawal Over Referendum
events.summary: Former DRC president Joseph Kabila's Front for the Refoundation of the Nation, which absorbed the AFC/M23 coalition, has assumed the Doha peace framework obligations with Kinshasa. The coalition is now threatening to withdraw from the talks if DRC proceeds with a proposed constitutional referendum.

events.headline: Storm Bruna Leaves Madeira Residents Homeless as Storm Charles Threatens Iberia With 130km/h Winds
events.summary: Storm Bruna brought flooding to Madeira, leaving ten people homeless and one still missing; a second system, Storm Charles, is forecast to bring heavy rain and gusts of up to 130 km/h to Madeira, mainland Portugal and Spain through Nov 11-13, prompting orange weather alerts.

events.headline: Qatar's PM to Meet Trump at White House Over Iran Diplomacy and Gaza Peace Plan
events.summary: Qatar's Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani is scheduled to meet Trump at the White House on Nov 10 to discuss Iran diplomacy and ceasefire mediation. Trump reportedly pressed Netanyahu by phone on Nov 5 to advance implementation of the Gaza peace plan.

events.headline: Georgia Opens Investigation After Uncounted Votes Flip State House Race
events.summary: Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger opened a formal investigation after a memory card holding about 388 uncounted votes surfaced in Seminole County, flipping House District 154 from Democrat Harry James to Republican Gerald Greene, who now leads by 262 votes. The late upload has raised questions about the county's election-night procedures.

events.headline: Train Collision Near El Ayyat, Giza Kills Seven, Injures Over 100 in Egypt
events.summary: A passenger train from Giza to Faiyum collided with the rear of a stationary train on the Cairo-Aswan line near El Ayyat, derailing multiple cars. At least 7 people were killed, including the driver, and more than 100 injured; President Sisi ordered an investigation amid domestic calls for the transport minister's resignation.

events.headline: Sudan Army-RSF Fighting Intensifies in West Kordofan; Ethiopia Expels Sudanese Diplomats
events.summary: Fighting intensified between Sudan's army and the RSF in West Kordofan, with the army claiming territorial gains and downing a fourth drone in a week, while RSF-allied forces claim to have captured a military base in Blue Nile state. Ethiopia expelled six Sudanese consular staff after Sudan accused Addis Ababa of hosting RSF drone-launch sites, prompting Sudan to reciprocate.

events.headline: Xavier Becerra Elected California Governor, First Latino Governor Since 1875
events.summary: Democrat Xavier Becerra defeated Republican Steve Hilton 65.2%-34.8% on Nov 3 to become California's 41st governor, succeeding term-limited Gavin Newsom. He is the first Latino elected governor of California since Romualdo Pacheco in 1875.

events.headline: Le Pen and Mélenchon Lead Early 2027 French Presidential Polling as Lecornu Accelerates Minimum-Wage Hike
events.summary: A new poll shows Marine Le Pen (34-36%) and Jean-Luc Mélenchon (18-19%) consolidating leads for the first round of France's 2027 presidential race. Separately, PM Sébastien Lecornu, facing weeks of cost-of-living protests, announced bringing forward a 1.6% minimum-wage increase from January to December after talks with unions, though unions called the raise insufficient.

events.headline: Amy Klobuchar Elected Minnesota's First Woman Governor as Democrats Win Full Trifecta
events.summary: Sitting US Sen. Amy Klobuchar defeated Republican Lisa Demuth 55.5%-42.6% on Nov 3 to become Minnesota's first woman governor. Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan won the open US Senate seat, and Democrats broke a 67-67 tie in the state House to secure full trifecta control of Minnesota government.

events.headline: Philadelphia Foster Mother Charged with Murder of 10-Year-Old Girl
events.summary: Carprice Williams was charged with murder in the death of 10-year-old foster child Malayshia Alford, whose body was found in Lindenwold, New Jersey. A New Jersey medical examiner ruled the death a homicide caused by blunt force trauma; Williams was denied bail.

events.headline: 97 Rescued as Record Flash Flooding Hits North Georgia Mountain Towns
events.summary: Record flash flooding on the Toccoa/Ocoee River prompted 97 water rescues in McCaysville, Georgia, with no confirmed fatalities, though one death was reported in neighboring Gilmer County pending confirmation. Gov. Brian Kemp declared a state of emergency for four counties as recovery continues.

events.headline: German 'Gen Z' Protests Turn Violent in Frankfurt and Other Cities, More Planned Nov 14
events.summary: The 'Gen Z regelt' youth movement organized demonstrations in about 34 German cities with roughly 120,000 participants on Oct 31. Protests in Frankfurt and elsewhere turned violent on Nov 1, with looting, smashed windows and injured police; further demonstrations are planned for Nov 14 and a student strike on Nov 20.

events.headline: Utah Mink Farm Expected to Lose 80% of Herd to Uncontrolled H5N1 Bird Flu
events.summary: C&T Fenn Farms south of Salt Lake City is expected to lose about 80% of its mink to an H5N1 outbreak from the same B3.13 strain lineage behind the US dairy cattle outbreak, after regulators declined to mandate culling. Alarm has renewed following a bird flu death reported in Washington state on Nov 6.

events.headline: COP31 UN Climate Conference Opens in Antalya, Türkiye, Running Through Nov 20
events.summary: The COP31 UN Climate Change Conference formally opened in Antalya, Türkiye on Nov 9 and will run through Nov 20. Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum is COP President, with Australian minister Chris Bowen co-presiding; a world leaders' summit is scheduled for Nov 11-12 with about 100,000 participants expected.

events.headline: Missouri Voters Reject Abortion and Trans-Care Ban as Democrats Break GOP Supermajority
events.summary: Missouri's Amendment 3, which would have imposed a near-total abortion ban and barred gender-affirming care for minors, failed with about 55% voting no on Nov 3. Democrats also flipped 16 Missouri House seats, their largest gain since 1974, breaking the GOP's veto-proof two-thirds supermajority though Republicans retain an overall majority.

events.headline: Mexico Captures CJNG Cell Leader 'El R2' in Jalisco Operation, 19 Others Detained
events.summary: Mexican forces arrested Rafael Álvarez Ayala, alias 'El R2,' a CJNG cell leader, in Zapopan, Jalisco, after an armed confrontation. A nationwide operation using CNI and DEA intelligence led to the detention of 19 other suspects.

events.headline: Kenyan Court Sentences Shakahola Cult Leader Paul Mackenzie to 200 Years
events.summary: A Kenyan court sentenced Shakahola cult leader Paul Mackenzie to a cumulative 200 years in prison on Nov 6 for the deaths of 190 children and one adult through starvation and direct homicide. Twenty-eight co-accused were also convicted, receiving sentences ranging from 10 to 160 years, in a broader tragedy believed to have killed over 400 people.

events.headline: Palm Bay, Florida Digs Out from Deadly Floods That Killed Two, Opened Sinkhole
events.summary: Record rainfall of up to 24 inches triggered a flash flood emergency in Palm Bay and Melbourne, Florida, killing two people, Joshua Bennett, 34, and Archie Richards, 78, and prompting more than 60 rescues. A large sinkhole in Palm Bay Estates destroyed a road and water main, leaving a boil-water advisory in effect.

events.headline: Federal Government Approves New $15-18 Billion Chesapeake Bay Bridge
events.summary: The Maryland Transportation Authority and Federal Highway Administration published a final environmental review and Record of Decision for two new four-lane spans across the Chesapeake Bay, estimated to cost $14.8-17.6 billion. Design work is set to begin around 2028, with construction targeted for 2032.

events.headline: South Africa's ANC Vote Share Collapses to 30.76% in Municipal Elections, Ending Dominance
events.summary: South Africa's ANC national vote share fell to 30.76% from 45.59% in 2021 in Nov 4 municipal elections, with official results confirmed Nov 8, while the DA rose to 24.64%. Hung councils rose to 142 from 70 in 2021, ending the ANC's uncontested dominance in many municipalities including Johannesburg.

events.headline: US Lame-Duck Congress Faces Dec 11 Shutdown Deadline Amid Push to Impeach Hegseth
events.summary: Congress returned for a lame-duck session following Republicans' midterm losses, facing a Dec 11 government funding deadline and an impeachment push against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth filed by outgoing Rep. Thomas Massie over Iran-strike and Caribbean boat-strike actions. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said he would be a 'hard yes' on impeachment.

events.headline: Myanmar Military Jet Bombs Resistance-Run Hospital in Sagaing Region, Killing Health Workers
events.summary: A Myanmar military jet bombed a resistance-operated hospital in Hlyawhpyukone village, Kawlin Township, Sagaing Region, on Nov 4, killing several healthcare workers including a senior doctor, with death tolls reported between five and eight. The UN has demanded an investigation into the attack.

events.headline: Pakistani Forces Repel Border Infiltration in Kurram as Bank Alfalah Completes Afghanistan Exit
events.summary: Pakistan's Bank Alfalah completed its exit from Afghanistan effective Nov 5, transferring its Kabul and Herat branches to Ghazanfar Bank after more than 20 years. Separately, Pakistani forces reported repelling an armed infiltration attempt by militants in Kurram's Shalozan sector, alleging covering fire from Afghan Taliban border forces, which Pakistan says it struck in response.

events.headline: Ransomware Attack Disrupts All 66 Queens Public Library Branches in New York City
events.summary: A ransomware attack discovered around Nov. 4 took down Queens Public Library's website, Wi-Fi, checkout systems, app and digital media across all 66 branches. Branches remained open while the NYPD and FBI investigate; restoration work is ongoing.

events.headline: Four People Killed in House Fire in Grand Meadow, Minnesota
events.summary: A fire at a single-family home in Grand Meadow killed four people on the morning of Nov. 8. The Mower County Sheriff's Office, state fire marshal and Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension are investigating; victims had not yet been identified.

events.headline: Record Flooding Causes Major Highway Damage Near Pagosa Springs, Colorado
events.summary: October 2026 storms pushed the San Juan River to its highest level since 1911, destroying or damaging bridges and causing more than $65 million in damage across roughly 100 miles of US-160 between Durango and South Fork. Recovery efforts are continuing into November.

events.headline: Families Sue Ohio Hospitals Over Doctor's Alleged Trove of Child Exploitation Images
events.summary: A federal lawsuit filed on behalf of 13 children alleges former Toledo pediatric urologist Bryan Sack kept a Dropbox account with more than 27,000 files, including child sexual abuse material and genital images of patients. Families are seeking over $5 million and class-action status covering up to 2,500 patients, naming Nationwide Children's Hospital and Mercy Health St. Vincent as defendants.

events.headline: Arkansas AG Moves to End 1991 Consent Decree Creating Black-Majority Judicial Districts
events.summary: Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin filed a federal motion on Nov 5 to terminate the 1991 Hunt v. Arkansas consent decree, which created Black-majority judicial subdistricts in the state. The NAACP Legal Defense Fund has said it will oppose the move.

events.headline: Ecuador: Thousands Protest Pretrial Detention of Opposition Leader Luisa González; Flooding Forces Evacuations in Milagro
events.summary: Thousands marched in Quito, Guayaquil and Cuenca on Nov 7 demanding President Daniel Noboa's resignation and the release of opposition leader Luisa González, held in pretrial detention since late October in a money-laundering case she calls political persecution. Separately, flooding from overflowing rivers forced evacuations and school closures in Milagro, Guayas province, prompting a government aid delivery.

events.headline: Virginia Becomes First Southern State to Repeal Same-Sex Marriage Ban
events.summary: Virginia voters repealed the 2006 Marshall-Newman Amendment on Nov. 3, passing a replacement recognizing marriage as a fundamental right by roughly 57%-43%. The change takes effect Jan. 1, 2027 upon certification, making Virginia the first Southern state to enshrine marriage equality.

events.headline: Gunmen Kill 11 Relatives of Vigilante, Abduct 13 Others in Zamfara, Nigeria
events.summary: Gunmen attacked the home of a government-backed vigilante volunteer in Gidan Taba village, Maradun LGA, after he helped security forces resist gang incursions, barricading and setting the home ablaze, killing 11 occupants. Thirteen others were abducted; security forces have since deployed to the area.

events.headline: Russian Strike Kills Three at Odesa Food Warehouse Day Before Abu Dhabi Peace Talks
events.summary: A Russian strike on Odesa killed three people and wounded one, setting ablaze a warehouse storing food supplies for the city's kindergartens and schools, roughly 24 hours before the start of US-brokered trilateral peace talks in Abu Dhabi.

events.headline: Serbia's New Parliament to Convene Nov 17 After Student List Election Win; Vučić's Last-Day Pardons Face Legal Challenge
events.summary: Serbia's new 250-seat parliament, in which the student-led 'Student List' won 140 seats against the SNS-led list's 103, will hold its first session Nov 17. Separately, 49 pardons issued by Aleksandar Vučić on his last day as president — including of a man charged with attempted murder of a protester — are under investigation by Serbia's organized-crime prosecutor.

events.headline: China's October Trade Surplus Tops $1 Trillion for Second Straight Year as Exports Surge 35.2%
events.summary: China's October exports rose 35.2% year-on-year, beating forecasts, driven by AI-hardware and integrated-circuit shipments, pushing the year-to-date trade surplus above $1.04 trillion for a second consecutive year; imports also surged 41.6%, narrowing the monthly surplus from September's level.

events.headline: Jury Deliberates in Federal Murder Trial of Ex-Officer Over Sandra Birchmore Death
events.summary: A federal jury began deliberating Nov. 6 in the trial of former Stoughton, Massachusetts officer Matthew Farwell, accused of killing pregnant 23-year-old Sandra Birchmore in 2021 and staging her death as a suicide. Deliberations resumed Nov. 9 in Boston.

events.headline: Audi Weighs $3 Billion Expansion of Planned EV Plant Near Macon, Georgia
events.summary: Georgia state documents show Audi is considering a second phase, worth about $3 billion and 3,000 jobs, at its planned $4 billion EV plant near Macon. The expansion would push the total investment toward roughly $7 billion.

events.headline: South Carolina Democrats Flip 10 House Seats, Breaking GOP Supermajority
events.summary: In the Nov. 3-4 election, South Carolina Democrats flipped 10 state House seats, including ousting Majority Leader Micah Caskey, ending the Republican supermajority in the chamber. The result shifts the balance of power in Columbia heading into 2027.

events.headline: Illinois House Speaker Chris Welch to Step Aside Amid Democratic Caucus Revolt
events.summary: Facing a revolt from 26 current and incoming House Democrats over his handling of sexual harassment allegations, Illinois House Speaker Chris Welch announced Nov. 5 he will not seek another term. Welch will step aside as speaker when the new legislature convenes in January.

events.headline: Arkansas Democrats Break Decade-Long GOP Supermajority in State House
events.summary: In the Nov. 3 midterms, Arkansas Democrats flipped seats, reducing the Republican House majority from 80-20 to roughly 69-30 and ending a three-fourths supermajority held since 2016. The shift gives Democrats new leverage over budget legislation.

events.headline: Bill Filing Opens for Texas's 2027 Legislature Under First Divided Government in Decades
events.summary: Bill filing opened Nov. 9 for the 90th Texas Legislature's 2027 session, the first under Democratic Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa, with Democrats now controlling the House and Republicans retaining the Senate. The divided government marks a major shift in Texas politics.

events.headline: About 800 Portland City Workers Begin Strike Over Pay
events.summary: Roughly 800 members of the City of Portland Professional Workers Union, including 911 dispatchers and emergency management and police/fire support staff, went on strike at 12:01 a.m. Nov. 9 after mediation failed. The dispute centers on pay, with the union seeking about 7% versus the city's lower offer.

events.headline: Washington Judge Orders Albertsons to Pay $900 Million Over Opioid Crisis Role
events.summary: King County Superior Court Judge Janet Helson ruled that Albertsons must pay $800 million in abatement funds plus a $100 million civil penalty, the largest verdict in Washington state history. The case centered on pharmacies dispensing more than 641 million opioid pills from 2006 to 2022 without adequate monitoring.

events.headline: Court Strikes Down Approval of California's First Major Carbon Capture Project
events.summary: A Kern County Superior Court judge ruled Nov. 3 that the county's approval of California Resources Corp's Carbon TerraVault I project violated the California Environmental Quality Act. The court ordered the county to withdraw its certification pending adequate environmental review.

events.headline: Trump Says Midterm Losses Partly Driven by Voter 'Dislike' for Israel Policy, Gas Prices
events.summary: In a CBS '60 Minutes' interview, Trump said he did not disagree that the Iran war hurt Republicans in the Nov 3 midterms, citing a 'great dislike' for Israel among voters and rising gas prices. He has previously vowed no change to his policy course after Democrats retook the House and Senate.

events.headline: Asian Stocks Rally Sharply as Semiconductor Rebound Lifts Nikkei, KOSPI After Taiwan's Earlier 5% Surge
events.summary: Japan's Nikkei rose roughly 2.5-3% and South Korea's KOSPI climbed as much as 4-5%, triggering a circuit breaker in one session, driven by a rebound in AI/semiconductor stocks following a surge in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index; SoftBank, SK Hynix and Samsung all gained strongly, extending the tech-led rally that had already lifted Taiwan's market 5% earlier in the week.

events.headline: Second Firefighting Helicopter Crashes in Indonesia's Worst Wildfire Season in a Decade, One Killed
events.summary: A BNPB-operated Super Puma helicopter crashed into the Barito River in South Kalimantan while collecting water for wildfire operations, killing one Indonesian crew member while two foreign pilots survived. It is a second, distinct crash in Indonesia's wildfire season after an earlier Mi-17 crash in Central Kalimantan killed three; South Kalimantan has since suspended aerial firefighting.

events.headline: Japan's Household Spending Plunges 6.8% in September, Steepest Drop Since 2020
events.summary: Japan's household spending fell 6.8% year-on-year in September, far below expectations, marking a 10th consecutive monthly decline and the sharpest drop since 2020, driven by weakness in transport, education, utilities and healthcare spending; officials partly blamed poor weather, while markets still expect a BOJ rate hike in December.

events.headline: France Confirms First-Ever Human Case of Shamonda Virus, Previously Found Only in Livestock
events.summary: French health authorities reported the first-ever human infection with Shamonda virus in a severely immunocompromised patient who died in early October, believed infected via a midge bite in eastern France, where the virus has circulated in livestock since spring 2026. ECDC says no risk to the general population has been identified to date.

events.headline: Germany's Merz Warns of 'Historic Test' Over Rising Antisemitism on Kristallnacht Anniversary
events.summary: Speaking at Munich's Ohel Jakob Synagogue on the 88th anniversary of Kristallnacht, Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Germany faces a 'historic test' over antisemitism he called 'once again omnipresent' in schools, streets and parliaments, decrying the need for armed protection at synagogues and kindergartens and pledging stronger government action.

events.headline: Canada's 2026 Budget Pledges Sovereign AI Compute as Parks Canada Warns of Nearly 3,000 Job Cuts
events.summary: Canada's Budget 2026 commits to 500MW of sovereign AI compute capacity. Separately, Parks Canada notified about 2,917 employees of potential job cuts tied to a federal expenditure review requiring C$144.9 million in savings over three years.

events.headline: Taiwan Detains Communist Party Leader Over Alleged China-Sponsored Vote-Buying
events.summary: Taiwanese prosecutors detained Lin Te-wang, leader of the Taiwan People's Communist Party, on Nov 8, alleging he ran borough-chief candidates and arranged China trips for voters as part of CCP-sponsored vote-buying ahead of Nov 28 local elections. Fourteen people have been summoned and nine witnesses questioned.

events.headline: Germany's Merz Backs Ilse Aigner to Become First Female President
events.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced support for Ilse Aigner, speaker of the Bavarian state parliament, to become Germany's next president and its first woman to hold the office. The CDU/CSU endorsement effectively guarantees her election by the Federal Convention on Jan 30, 2027.

events.headline: North Korea Tests New Air Defense Missile and Cruise Missile in Fourth Weapons Drill in a Month
events.summary: North Korean state media reported tests of a new anti-aircraft and surface-to-air missile system, along with a separate cruise-missile drill simulating a cluster-munition strike on an enemy airport runway targeting more than 20 aircraft-shaped mock targets. It marks the fourth North Korean weapons-launch event in a month.

events.headline: Two Egyptian Border Guard Officers Killed Near Sudan Border in Clash With Illegal Gold Miners
events.summary: Two Egyptian army border-guard officers were killed in an exchange of fire during an operation targeting illegal gold-mining groups near Egypt's southern border with Sudan in the Halayeb/Shalateen area. Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan and the Arab League issued condemnations and condolences.

events.headline: Brazil's Supreme Court Closes Seven-Year 'Fake News' Inquiry at Prosecutor-General's Request
events.summary: Brazil's Prosecutor-General Paulo Gonet asked the Supreme Federal Court (STF) to archive the seven-year 'fake news' inquiry opened in 2019 to probe threats against the Court, arguing its objective had been exhausted; STF President Edson Fachin granted the request the same day. The closure does not nullify evidence already gathered or invalidate derivative criminal cases still proceeding separately.

events.headline: Car Sinks in Lake Near Barra Mansa, Brazil, Killing All 10 Occupants Including Five Children
events.summary: A car overturned and sank into a lake near Barra Mansa in Rio de Janeiro state, killing all 10 people inside, including five children. Authorities are investigating the cause of the accident.

events.headline: Heavy Rains Flood Santa Elena Province in Ecuador, Forcing Family Evacuations
events.summary: Heavy rains flooded Colonche parish in Santa Elena province, Ecuador, as rivers overflowed near Cruce de Palmar. About 30 families were evacuated and roughly 150 families were affected provincewide, though no deaths were reported.

events.headline: Six Gulf States Sign Agreement to Advance Regional Railway Network by 2030
events.summary: Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar, the UAE and Oman signed an agreement in Manama on Nov 8 advancing the 2,117km Gulf railway network, currently 55.9% complete. The project targets passenger operations by December 2030, with capacity for 8 million passengers and 95 million tonnes of freight annually by 2045.

events.headline: Bomb Threat Forces Evacuation of The Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn
events.summary: A phoned-in bomb threat on the evening of Nov. 7 forced evacuation of a wedding reception and fundraiser at The Henry Ford museum. Dearborn police and a K-9 unit found no threat, and normal operations resumed Nov. 8.

events.headline: Louisiana Becomes Only US State With 'High' Flu Activity as Season Surges Early
events.summary: CDC and Louisiana Department of Health data show Louisiana is the only state with 'high' influenza-like-illness activity this season, with 4.3% of outpatient visits flu-related and a 10.9% test positivity rate versus a 7.6% national average. The early surge is being driven by H1N1.

events.headline: DNA Testing Identifies Three More 1999 Kosovo War Disappearance Victims From Mass Grave
events.summary: Kosovo PM Albin Kurti confirmed DNA analysis conducted at The Hague identified three more victims of enforced disappearance from the 1998-99 war — Adem Ademi, Fatmir Fazlija and Ali Haliti — among at least 23 people exhumed since July from mass graves near Zubin Potok in northern Kosovo. Roughly 1,600 people remain missing from the war overall.

events.headline: Magnitude 5.9 Earthquake Strikes Off Ibaraki Prefecture, Shakes Tokyo Region
events.summary: A preliminary magnitude 5.9 earthquake struck off Ibaraki Prefecture northeast of Tokyo, registering intensity 3 (of 7) in Miyagi, Ibaraki, Fukushima and Tochigi, with tremors felt in Tokyo. No tsunami warning was issued and no casualties or damage were reported.

events.headline: Nepal Police Detain Three Journalists in Kathmandu Newsroom Raids Over PM Corruption Reporting
events.summary: Plainclothes police raided several Kathmandu newsrooms and detained three journalists after their outlets reported that PM Balendra Shah sought the resignation of the police inspector general over alleged money-laundering ties; all three were released the same evening amid public backlash, and press-freedom groups held protest rallies demanding guarantees against future crackdowns.

events.headline: Bangladesh Reiterates Extradition Request for Ousted PM Sheikh Hasina From India
events.summary: Bangladesh's Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman publicly reiterated a formal extradition request to India for ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Nov 8, calling her a 'convicted criminal.' India has not announced a decision on the request.

events.headline: Encore Boston Harbor Workers End 63-Day Strike After Ratifying New Contract
events.summary: About 1,300 Encore Boston Harbor casino workers represented by UNITE HERE Local 26 and Teamsters Local 25 ratified a new contract on Nov. 5, ending a roughly two-month strike over pay, benefits and health care. Workers returned to the Everett, Massachusetts casino on Nov. 6.

events.headline: Connecticut Reports Earliest Flu Deaths of the Season in Recent Years
events.summary: Connecticut's health department reported six flu deaths, all among residents 55 and older, since late September 2026 — the earliest seasonal flu deaths in recent years. Officials are urging residents to get vaccinated amid an unusually aggressive early flu season.

events.headline: Rhode Island Voters Reject Statewide Bond Questions for First Time Since 2006
events.summary: On Nov. 3, Rhode Island voters rejected two of five statewide bond questions worth about $150 million combined while approving roughly $450 million in other borrowing. It was the state's first rejection of a bond question since 2006.

events.headline: Warehouse Fire Triggers Shelter-in-Place Near Moundsville, West Virginia
events.summary: A fire at Swierkos Enterprises Inc. prompted a shelter-in-place order on Nov. 8 in Marshall County and closed WV Route 2. The order was lifted by evening, though a nearby elementary school shifted to remote learning the following Monday.

events.headline: Pilot Killed in Vintage L-39 Jet Crash Near Mayfield, Kentucky
events.summary: A Wisconsin pilot died on Nov. 8 when a vintage L-39 Albatros jet crashed and caught fire shortly after takeoff from Mayfield-Graves County Airport. The FAA and NTSB are investigating the cause of the crash.

events.headline: Lawsuit Presses to Invalidate Virginia's Newly Approved Reproductive Rights Amendment
events.summary: After Virginia voters approved a reproductive-rights constitutional amendment on Nov. 3 with about 62% support, conservative legal group Liberty Counsel is pursuing an appeal challenging a procedural step in how the measure reached the ballot. The case could affect the amendment's validity.

events.headline: Winnebago Industries Cuts 51 More Jobs at Forest City, Iowa Plant
events.summary: Winnebago Industries filed a WARN notice for 51 layoffs effective around Nov. 9 at its Forest City, Iowa plant, bringing total 2026 cuts there to 78. The company is shifting production to its facility in Middlebury, Indiana.

events.headline: Former Arkansas Bar-Exam Administrator Charged with 65 Felony Records Tampering Counts
events.summary: Nancie Givens, former director of the Arkansas Office of Professional Programs, was charged Nov. 5 with 65 felony counts of tampering with public records over alleged alteration and destruction of bar-exam records from 2020 to 2025. She pleaded not guilty and was released on $2,500 bond.

events.headline: Oklahoma Regulators Approve 3.55% Residential Rate Increase for PSO
events.summary: The Oklahoma Corporation Commission voted 2-1 on Nov. 5 to approve a 3.55% residential electricity rate increase for Public Service Company of Oklahoma. The new rates take effect in December 2026.

events.headline: Federal Judge Rules Army Corps Unlawfully Approved Gold-Dredging Permit Near Nome
events.summary: US District Judge Sharon Gleason ruled Nov. 6 that the Army Corps of Engineers' Pacific Division violated NEPA and the Clean Water Act in approving a gold-dredging permit near an ecologically sensitive estuary near Nome, Alaska. Remedy briefing in the case is due Nov. 24.

events.headline: Chile's Inflation Hits 4.5%, Highest in Over a Year, as President Kast's Approval Sinks to Record Low
events.summary: Chile's annual inflation rose to 4.5% in October, above the central bank's target, driven by fuel and food costs. President José Antonio Kast's approval has sunk to roughly 26-29%, driven by anger over the early release of convicted child sex offenders and a stagnant economy.

events.headline: Magnitude 6.4 Earthquake Strikes Near Lata, Solomon Islands; No Casualties Reported
events.summary: A shallow magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck about 27km southwest of Lata, Temotu Province, Solomon Islands. USGS issued a Green alert indicating low likelihood of casualties or damage; an estimated 12,000 people felt strong shaking, but no casualties or damage were reported.
